_note: Railways (plan: project files steam_trains/plan.md). Placeholder numbers, Tim to tune. route: cost per world terrain code for laying track (m and w are impassable); bridge = river and water cells the track may cross; maxBridge = longest crossing in world units; reuse = cost factor on cells that already carry your track (branching); simplify = how far (world units) the drawn line may stray from the cell path; smooth = corner-rounding passes; clearance and minRadius: see _clearance.

route._clearance: Tim 2026-11-07: track keeps clearance world units (one town cell) from mountains and other impassable cells, in the world and in towns; minRadius = tightest curve in world units (corners are rounded to arcs, no hairpins)

link._note: placeholder, Tim to tune. A link is the whole track between two stations and always takes seconds to lay, whatever its length; paid a stretch at a time from the ordering town's stock (costPer100 per 100 units of track; waits when the stock runs short); minTier = town hall tier a town needs before it can link; maxBuilding = links one clan may lay at once.
link._campCostNote: 8e-4 (2026-11-16), placeholder: a war camp's spur is paid from the camp stores, which hold no goods, so stone stands in for the goods share.

gang._note: placeholder: the rail gang drawn at the railhead (laborers; real units only near someone on the island, like town workers). hammerSeconds = how long they work in place before walking up to the railhead again; anim = rail_worker = laborer body holding a sledge (tools/export_sprites.mjs ITEMS); work clip hammer = Great Sword Slash swing.

ship._note: Rail shipments (Tim 2026-11-08), placeholders, Tim to tune. keep = default stock a town never ships out (per resource; later: upkeep plus next build); minOrder = smallest order; queueTrips (Tim 2026-11-09) = your own undelivered orders into a town may add up to this many trainloads per line at the town (trainload = goods wagons x wagonLoad; 3 x 240 = 720 (Tim 2026-11-17: wagons carry double, 120 each), about 3 round trips, ~11 min on a capital line); maxAuto = open auto orders per town; budget = default auto-buy ryo per town at the port (a town may have this much tied up in open auto orders); buyPrice / sellPrice = ryo per unit at the port wholesale houses (buying costs more than selling pays); sell = spare goods go to the capital once the store is above aboveShare full, batch at a time; keepMax = highest keep a player can set.
ship._ryoNote: 8e-1 (2026-11-16), placeholders: ryoPerTrain = ryo one train carries (guard car, no wagon room); ryoMin = smallest ryo order.

overflow._note: placeholder (Tim 2026-11-17): the governor sells timber and stone only when the store is full (at = share of storage), down to downTo of storage, never while a war is on the town or it fills a war camp order; food is never sold on its own

ship._keepShare: default keep amount = this share of the town storage cap per resource (goods too: market hold-back); a keep the player sets wins

train._note: placeholder, Tim to tune. Each open link gets one train (stand-in until stations build them): it runs station to station and back at speed (world units a second; the hero runs at 6), waiting stopSeconds at each end (Tim 2026-11-07: 60, long enough to walk over and board). cars = carriages and wagons behind the engine; gap = world units from one car's middle to the next (engine first). viewSpeed (Tim 2026-11-07) = its speed while someone rides it or a player hero is within viewRange of the engine (a little under a horse, 22.5); with nobody near it runs at speed, so arrival times hold.
train._consist: Tim 2026-11-07: the cars behind the engine and tender, front to back: carriage (8 seats each, ride.seatsPerCar), goods (goods wagon), guard (brake van). Drawn from the train_* sprites; replaces cars and gap where set.

ride._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (train plan step 4). Board at a station while the train stands there: you and your followers (within followRange) ride, and every standing Hero group crew within heroGroupRange, following or not (Tim 2026-11-07); seatsPerCar = riders per carriage (the engine, tender and last wagon carry none). The train leaves departSeconds after you board. skipSeconds = how long you ride before Skip takes you straight to the far station. The capital end lands you just inside the island gate. reach = how close to a town's station you must stand.
ride._boarding: Tim 2026-11-08: picking a train calls All aboard: a zone of zoneRadius on the ground round the station for callSeconds, or until the train leaves if sooner; everyone of yours in it then gets on, Space again boards at once. followRange and heroGroupRange are no longer used.

robbery._note: Train robbery (Tim 2026-11-20, plan war_build/train_robbery/plan.md). R1 blasting: a hero standing within reach of any open line (anyone's, war or not) sets a charge; it blows after fuseSeconds. The line is closed closeDays (game days) while an untouchable repair crew (crew.size, model, anim; real units only within crew.spawnRadius of someone) hammers at the gap, and can't be blown or robbed again for cooldownDays from the blast. Not within 2 x stopGap of a station. A train running into the gap stops stopGap short of it, stands stopSeconds, then backs up to the last station it passed.
robbery._robbery: R2-R3 (Tim 2026-11-20): guards[faction] = the war roster units (frontier.json war.units) that get out of a train stopped at a blown track, round its freight wagon; the fallen are missing until it next reaches a station. A hero within wagonReach of the freight wagon of someone else's stopped train holds holdSeconds (placeholder) to take share of everything aboard, once per blast, into a stolen chest. Knocked out, the hero drops it; any hero picks it up within pickReach; cash it within cashReach of an own town hall or war camp banner. A dropped chest is gone after chestDays (placeholder). Guards attack any enemy they see within guardAggro and chase up to guardLeash from their spot (placeholders, Tim 2026-11-21: hyper aggressive).

bots._note: placeholder, Tim 2026-11-20 (train robbery R5, sim/war_general_brain.js): days = game days between a bot's robberies by its war strategy, [least, most], in a war and in peace (Raider about once a day or two in war; the others rarely). In a war it robs only that war's enemy inside the war circle (camp supply lines first) with escort war troops (escortMin or it waits); in peace it needs peaceCrew crew at the hero's side. reach = how far the hero walks to a line; waitSeconds beside the line for a loaded train (minLoad cargo); the hero starts the hold when holdGuards or fewer guards stand; maxSeconds for the whole try; retryDays before trying again after giving up. Any general sends up to defenders war troops within defendReach to its own train stopped at a blown track inside its war circle. A bot hero picks up a dropped chest within grabReach.
